backlog.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic constraint Jacobian (pair distance, wall and positivity rows) to minimize(). This removes finite-difference cost (about 78 variables) so many more restarts or iterations fit in the time budget. Build the Jacobian with numpy using precomputed iu index arrays.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Set MAX_ITER=1000 so SLSQP converges fully instead of stopping at 200 iterations. Also add ftol=1e-12 in options. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Raise MAX_ITER to 1000

backlog.spec: Run many restarts with MAX_ITER=60. Keep the top 5 by sum of radii after repair. Re-run SLSQP from each of them (warm start with the current centres and radii) with maxiter=500, and return the best.
backlog.title: Two-phase: short screening, long polish

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random start with a jittered 5x5 grid plus one extra circle (26 points). Add Gaussian noise of sd 0.03 to the centres. Use a start radius of about 0.08. Structured starts are closer to good packings.
backlog.title: Grid-perturbed initialization

backlog.spec: Initialize centres from staggered rows (for example row counts 5,5,5,5,6 or 6,5,6,5,4) over the unit square with small jitter. Pick the row pattern at random per restart.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice initialization

backlog.spec: After an initial batch of restarts, spend the remaining time perturbing the best solution. Move 2-4 random circles to new random positions, or add noise sd 0.02 to all centres. Re-optimize with SLSQP and accept if better.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from best

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping stage, swap the positions of two circles with different radii. Set the radii to the mean and re-optimize. This explores permutation-like rearrangements.
backlog.title: Swap-large-small perturbation

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9. Make sure repair and overhead are small, and check that CPU time stays well below 45 s.
backlog.title: Use the whole time budget

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.02 so that the starting point is feasible and SLSQP grows radii from a feasible state. Try INIT_LOW=0.05 as well.
backlog.title: Smaller initial radius

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii uniformly from 0.03-0.12 instead of a constant, to diversify the size distributions that the optimizer explores.
backlog.title: Random initial radii

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative pairwise repair with a global approach. First clip the radii to the walls. Then for each violating pair shrink only as much as is needed, repeating until no violation remains. Finally subtract 1e-12 rather than 1e-9 (the tolerance is 1e-10). This gains about 1e-9 per circle, which is tiny but free.
backlog.title: Better repair: exact scaling

backlog.spec: With the centres fixed, solve a linear program (scipy linprog) that maximizes the sum of radii. The constraints are r_i+r_j<=d_ij-1e-12 and r_i<=wall distance. This gives the optimal feasible radii for those centres and replaces the heuristic repair.
backlog.title: LP radius refit after optimizing

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, iterate the cycle LP radius refit then SLSQP with small steps, to converge to a strict local optimum with active constraints satisfied to 1e-12.
backlog.title: Trust-constr / active-set polish

backlog.spec: Keep the pair constraints only for pairs whose centre distance is below 0.45 at the start of a polish run. Rebuild the constraint set every few runs. This shrinks the SLSQP problem from 325 pair constraints and speeds up each iteration.
backlog.title: Only near-neighbour constraints

backlog.spec: Use the smooth form (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0 with a Jacobian instead of sqrt. This avoids the sqrt singularity at zero distance and gives better SLSQP behaviour.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run 100-200 steps of L-BFGS-B on a penalty energy: -sum r + mu*sum of squared overlaps and wall violations, with mu increasing. Then hand the result to SLSQP. This gives better-conditioned starts.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: First solve with maximize sum r^p with p=2 or 0.5 for some iterations to bias the sizes, then switch to p=1. This diversifies the local optima found.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted objective annealing

backlog.spec: Generate starts that are symmetric under reflection about the diagonal or about the vertical axis: sample 13 points and mirror them. Add noise. Many good packings are near-symmetric.
backlog.title: Symmetry-seeded starts

backlog.spec: Express the wall constraints as variable bounds: r>=0, r<=0.5, and centres in [0,1]. Keep only the wall-distance inequalities that are still needed, which reduces the constraint count and speeds up SLSQP.
backlog.title: Bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: Keep the top 8 solutions. Create a new start by taking circles in the left half from one elite and the right half from another, then fill to n circles by dropping or adding random ones. Optimize and update the pool.
backlog.title: Elite pool with recombination

backlog.spec: In the improvement stage, delete the circle with the smallest radius. Reinsert it at the largest empty spot, found by sampling 2000 random points and taking the one with maximum clearance. Re-optimize.
backlog.title: Remove-smallest and reinsert

backlog.spec: Run 40 SLSQP iterations first. If the sum of radii is below 97% of the best so far, abandon the restart. Otherwise continue to 300 iterations. This cuts wasted time.
backlog.title: Early-abort of poor restarts

backlog.spec: Spend 50% of the time on diverse random restarts and 50% on basin hopping of the top 3 solutions, divided equally among them.
backlog.title: Dedicated seed-fraction split

backlog.spec: Initialize with a mix: 4 large circles (r 0.12) near the corners, about 12 medium (0.1) and the rest small (0.06). Use jittered positions. This mimics the structure of the best known packings.
backlog.title: Sorted-radius size-class init

backlog.spec: Sample initial centres from a Beta(0.7,0.7) distribution so that points cluster near the borders and corners. The best packings put large circles at the boundaries.
backlog.title: Corner-biased initial centres

backlog.spec: Compute the iu indices and the constraint scaffolding once, outside the loop, and reuse them. Also use a squared-distance form to cut Python overhead per function evaluation. This gives more restarts.
backlog.title: Cache pair index arrays and vectorize

backlog.spec: For the best solution, repeatedly add noise sd 0.005 to the centres, shrink the radii by 10%, and re-run SLSQP with maxiter 150. Accept if the sum improves. This does local-neighbourhood exploration.
backlog.title: Shake with small noise and re-solve

backlog.spec: In the last 10% of the time, run SLSQP on the best solution with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=1000, with constraints tightened by a margin of 1e-11. Then repair. Keep the result only if the sum is higher.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish

backlog.spec: Make the SLSQP constraints require distance >= r_i+r_j+2e-11 and the walls with the same margin. The repair then does almost nothing, so no solution loses radius to the 50-iteration repair loop, which sometimes fails to converge.
backlog.title: Constraint margin to avoid repair loss

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in 3 stages of 50 iterations. Between stages, add Gaussian noise to the centres, with sd 0.01, then 0.005, then 0. Warm-start the radii at 90% of their values.
backlog.title: Annealed center jitter during SLSQP restarts

backlog.spec: After about 30% of the time spent on random restarts, switch to basin hopping. Take the best (c, r) found. Each iteration: copy it, pick 1-3 random circles and relocate them to random positions with radius 0.02 (or jitter all centres with sd 0.02), then run SLSQP from there with MAX_ITER=300 using radii initialised as 0.9*r. Accept if the repaired sum is larger than the current best (or with small Metropolis probability). Continue until the time budget is used. Keep the best valid packing.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from best with local perturbation

backlog.spec: After SLSQP and clipping in each restart, fix the centres and solve an LP with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) that maximises sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= wall distances, r >= 0. Use the result (minus 1e-12 margin) instead of the heuristic _repair shrink. This recovers the loss from approximate feasibility and gives the exact optimal radii for the centres. Keep _repair only as a fallback if the LP fails.
backlog.title: Constrained LP radius refit plus polish

backlog.spec: Build initial centres from structured layouts: with probability 0.5 use a hex-like lattice with rows of 5,5,5,5,6 or 6,5,6,5,4 style counts (choose randomly among row-count patterns summing to 26), scaled into the square, with Gaussian jitter sd 0.02, and radii init 0.08. Otherwise use the existing random start. Everything else is unchanged. Seeds control the pattern and jitter.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice and perturbed-grid starts mixed with random

backlog.spec: Run many short SLSQP restarts (MAX_ITER=40) for about 40% of the time and record the raw objective of each result. Keep the top 5 by objective (after the repair step). Spend the remaining time continuing SLSQP with MAX_ITER=500 from each of these in turn, warm-started from their end points, and return the best repaired packing.
backlog.title: Two-stage screening then long polish

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a cheap vectorised pre-relaxation: minimise sum over pairs of max(0, ri+rj-dij)^2 plus wall violations minus lambda*sum r with L-BFGS-B (analytic gradient via numpy) for lambda increasing through 3 stages (0.01, 0.03, 0.1). Use the result as SLSQP's start. This produces feasible-ish, well-spread starts and should reduce the number of wasted SLSQP iterations and poor local optima.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation with growing radii

backlog.spec: Keep an elite pool of the best 5 distinct packings. After 30% of the time, repeatedly pick an elite, choose the largest circle and a small circle, swap their centres (and radii), add jitter sd 0.01, shrink radii by 0.8, and re-run SLSQP. Add the result to the pool if it beats the worst elite. Return the best.
backlog.title: Swap-size perturbation of elite solutions

backlog.spec: Replace the 4n wall inequality constraints and r>=0 by SLSQP bounds: centre coordinates in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5], then keep only a wall constraint set as c - r >= 0 etc. only for circles whose initial centre is within 0.25 of that wall. Smaller constraint set speeds each SLSQP iteration so more restarts fit within the budget. Repair step handles any remaining violation.
backlog.title: Bounds for walls and halved constraint set

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5, generate a start with mirror symmetry: sample 13 centres in the left half x in [0,0.5], mirror them across x=0.5 to get 26 centres, with identical radii for the mirrored pairs, plus small jitter sd 0.005 to break exact degeneracy. Use this as the SLSQP start (the optimiser is free to desymmetrise). Alternatively use the diagonal mirror. Else use random start.
backlog.title: Symmetric-seeded starts

backlog.spec: In each restart, optimise with objective -sum(w_i r_i) where w_i are random in [0.7,1.3], for a first SLSQP run of 100 iterations. Then re-run SLSQP with true objective -sum r from that result for MAX_ITER=200. The random weights push the optimiser to different size distributions (big/small circle arrangements), diversifying local optima.
backlog.title: Annealed random radius weights in objective

backlog.spec: Run every restart first for only 60 SLSQP iterations. Compute the current radii sum (after clip and fast repair). Only if it exceeds the 60th percentile of the previous first-stage results (or the first 10 restarts are collected) continue the same solution with 300 more iterations, starting from the result. Otherwise discard. This concentrates compute on promising basins.
backlog.title: Early abort of poor restarts with warm continuation

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 9 structure (random restarts, then perturbation of the single best packing) but change the explore phase from 0.3 to 0.15 of the budget, so more time goes to refinement of the best packing. Measures the restart-fraction sensitivity; edit the 0.3 factor in the explore condition of solve().
backlog.title: Replicate slot 9 with 50% restart split

backlog.spec: After the main loop, run one more SLSQP from the best (c, r) with maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-14, then repair. Only accept it if the repaired sum exceeds the best. Reserve about 1.5 s of CPU for it by ending the main loop at 0.75 of the time limit.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish with tight tolerance

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, with probability 0.4, pick one of the largest 6 circles and one of the smallest 10 circles from the best packing and swap their centres, setting both radii to the mean of the two. Otherwise use the existing perturbation. Re-solve with SLSQP and keep the result if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Swap-large-small perturbation in refinement

backlog.spec: Replace the 4n wall inequality constraints and r>=0 with SLSQP variable bounds. Centres get bounds [0,1] and radii [0,0.5]. Add the wall constraints c-r>=0 only through the existing form if needed for validity, since bounds alone do not enforce them. If this is not clean, instead keep the wall constraints but drop the explicit r>=0 constraints and use bounds for r. The smaller constraint set should speed up each SLSQP iteration and allow more restarts.
backlog.title: Bounds for walls, drop wall constraints

backlog.spec: For 1/3 of the explore-phase restarts, initialise centres on a hex-like lattice (rows of 5 and 6 alternating, giving about 26 points, truncated or padded at random) scaled into [0.08, 0.92]. Add Gaussian noise of sd 0.02 and set the radii to 0.08. The remaining restarts stay uniform random. This seeds the search with structured near-optimal topologies.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice perturbed starts mixed in

backlog.spec: Run each explore restart as a short SLSQP with maxiter=60. Continue it to the full MAX_ITER only if the unrepaired radius sum is within 0.03 of the best sum so far. Otherwise discard it. This saves time on bad basins and allows many more restarts in the explore phase.
backlog.title: Early abort of poor restarts

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP in each explore restart, run about 30 steps of L-BFGS-B on a penalty energy: sum of squared pair overlaps plus wall violations, with radii fixed at a value that grows from 0.06 to 0.10 over 3 rounds. Use the result as the SLSQP start. This gives well-spread starts that avoid initial overlap tangles.
backlog.title: Penalty pre-relaxation with growing radii

backlog.spec: In the explore-phase SLSQP runs, use the objective -sum(w*r) with w = 1 + 0.3*U(-1,1) drawn per circle and per restart. Then do a final short SLSQP with w = 1 starting from the result. This perturbs the landscape to reach different basins, and the true objective is restored at the end.
backlog.title: Randomised radius weights in objective

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, keep a noise scale s starting at 0.01. Multiply s by 1.2 after a failure and by 0.8 after an improvement, clipped to [0.002, 0.05]. Use s as the centre noise sd for the perturbation, and also relocate 1 to 3 random circles with probability 0.3. Add the 1/5 rule style adaptation to the slot 9 loop.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation size with success feedback

backlog.spec: For 20% of explore restarts, draw 13 random centres and radii in the half-square or triangle and mirror them through the centre point (x,y)->(1-x,1-y) to give 26 circles. Add a small noise sd 0.005 and run SLSQP. Many best-known packings for this problem have approximate symmetry, so this halves the search dimension for those starts.
backlog.title: Symmetry-seeded starts

backlog.spec: Re-implement the slot 9 scheme exactly: 30% of the time budget on random restarts (existing explore logic), then perturb only the single best packing (swap/relocate 2-4 circles or gaussian noise sd 0.02, accept only if the repaired sum improves). Change nothing else except that the explore phase uses 0.3 of TIME_FRACTION, as now. Purpose: a clean replicate to confirm that the -2.6360 result is real.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 9 with 50% restart split removed

backlog.spec: For about half of the explore restarts, initialise the centres from a hexagonal-ish lattice. Use rows of 5,5,5,5,5,1 or 5,6,5,6,4 style staggered rows, take the first 26 points, scale them into [0.08,0.92], and add gaussian noise sd 0.03 plus a random rotation of the row layout. Set initial radii to 0.05. The other half stay uniform random.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice perturbed starts

backlog.spec: Drop the four wall-constraint blocks from cons. Instead pass SLSQP bounds: x and y in [0,1] and r in [0,0.5]. This leaves a constraint vector of only pair distances. Because wall distance c-r >= 0 is no longer enforced, keep the repair step as is, since it already clips radii to wall distance. Gives smaller QP subproblems and faster iterations.
backlog.title: Walls as bounds, not constraints

backlog.spec: Replace the _repair loop with a robust version: first clip radii to the wall distance, then iterate up to 200 times, each time computing all overlaps and shrinking every overlapping pair so that r_i+r_j equals d minus 1e-12. Once no overlap remains, stop. The old loop stops at 50 iterations and may leave overlaps, so this version also recovers sum loss from that and avoids crashes. Keep SHRINK at 1e-12 instead of 1e-9.
backlog.title: Exact repair by LP-free scaling

backlog.spec: For half of the explore restarts, run the first 80 SLSQP iterations with objective -sum(w*r) where w is uniform in [0.7,1.3] per circle, then continue with the true objective (maxiter 150) from that result. This pushes different circles to grow large and diversifies the basins reached.
backlog.title: Randomised radius-weight objective for diversity

backlog.spec: In the explore phase, run SLSQP with maxiter 40 first. Compute the sum of the radii at that point. Continue to 200 more iterations only if the sum is above the median of the previous short-run sums (or in the first 10 runs). This saves the time spent on bad starts without the separate screening phase used before. Keep the slot 9 refinement afterwards.
backlog.title: Early-abort short run then continue

backlog.spec: For one third of the explore restarts, generate 13 random points in the unit square and mirror them through the centre (x,y) -> (1-x,1-y) to get 26 points, with a small noise sd 0.01. Use radii of 0.05 and run SLSQP as usual. Many best known packings have approximate point or mirror symmetry, so this restricts the search to a promising subspace.
backlog.title: Symmetric-seeded starts

backlog.spec: Keep MAX_ITER 200 for explore restarts but use maxiter 600 for refinement-phase SLSQP calls (pass a maxiter argument to _solve_once). Refinement runs start near a good optimum and may stop before they converge, so the extra iterations let them reach the exact local optimum.
backlog.title: Larger MAX_ITER in refinement only

backlog.spec: Re-implement slot 9 exactly: explore with random restarts for 30% of the TIME_FRACTION budget, then for the remaining time repeatedly perturb only the single best packing (either relocate 2-4 circles to random spots with radius INIT_RADIUS*0.5, or add N(0,0.02) noise to centres), run SLSQP from it with radii*0.9, and accept only if the repaired sum improves. Change nothing else, purely to confirm the gain with a different noise draw. Use explore fraction 0.2 instead of 0.3 as the only variation.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 9 with 50% restart-free split

backlog.spec: Remove the four wall constraint blocks (c-r etc.) from cons and pass bounds to SLSQP instead: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Keep the pair constraints and the r>=0 handling through bounds. The repair step still clips radii to wall distance. This reduces the constraint count from 26*5+325 to 325 and speeds each SLSQP iteration, giving more basin-hopping steps in the same CPU time.
backlog.title: Walls as variable bounds

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 8% of the time budget. Run SLSQP on the best packing with maxiter=1000 and ftol=1e-15, starting from the best centres and radii (not shrunk). Repair it and keep the result only if its sum is larger than the current best. This squeezes out the last 1e-4 to 1e-3 that the 200-iteration runs leave on the table.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish of best

backlog.spec: Keep MAX_ITER=200 for the explore phase but use maxiter=500 for SLSQP runs started from the best packing in the refinement phase (add a parameter to _solve_once). Perturbed starts are near a good basin, so longer runs converge fully to the local optimum, which lowers repair loss.
backlog.title: Larger MAX_ITER in refinement only

backlog.spec: In explore mode, with probability 0.5 initialise centres from a hexagonal-like lattice: pick a random row layout (e.g. rows of 5,5,5,5,6 or 4,5,4,5,4,4 chosen at random with sum 26), spread rows evenly over [0.1,0.9], add N(0,0.03) noise, and set radii 0.05. The rest stay uniform random. Near-lattice starts land in the structured basins of the known best packings.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice perturbed starts

backlog.spec: In explore mode run SLSQP for 60 iterations first, repair and compute the sum. If it is below 0.985 of the best sum so far, discard it; otherwise continue SLSQP for 200 more iterations from that point and keep the result. Different from the earlier screening idea: this needs no top-k bookkeeping and applies to the explore phase only, so slot 9's refinement stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Early abort of poor restarts

backlog.spec: Require pair distances >= r_i+r_j+1e-9 and wall distances >= r+1e-9 inside the SLSQP constraint function, and set SHRINK to 0 in the repair (keep the overlap-fix loop and the final max(r,0)). Check that validity still holds to 1e-10 with the harness tolerance. This removes the systematic shrink of 26*1e-9 and any SLSQP feasibility slack.
backlog.title: Constraint margin to cut repair loss

backlog.spec: In explore mode with probability 0.3, generate 13 random circles in the half-square x<=0.5 with radius 0.05 and mirror them across x=0.5 to get 26 (or reflect across the diagonal). Optimise with SLSQP from this start without enforcing symmetry. Many best-known packings are near-symmetric, so this seeds good basins.
backlog.title: Symmetry-seeded starts

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase accept a perturbed result when its sum is >= best - 2e-4 (a small simulated-annealing threshold) but track the global best separately and return that. The current walker moves to the accepted solution, allowing drift across plateaus of near-equal packings. Reset the walker to the global best every 15 failures.
backlog.title: Bolder: two-circle-class greedy shaking with acceptance of equal moves

backlog.spec: For fresh explore restarts, the first SLSQP stage (60 iterations) maximises sum(w_i r_i) with w_i ~ uniform(0.5,1.5) drawn per restart. Then the second stage (up to 200 iterations) maximises the true sum r from that result. This diversifies topology of the contact graph, which breaks the symmetry of equal-weights starts. Use only for 50% of restarts.
backlog.title: Random-radius-weight objective for the first stage only

backlog.spec: Keep slot 9 logic (random restarts, then perturb the single best packing with acceptance only on improvement) but set the explore fraction to 0.25 of the used time and use fixed perturbation: 50% relocate 2-3 random circles to random positions with radius 0.03, 50% Gaussian centre noise sd 0.02. Purpose is to check that the gain is real and reduce variance.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 9 exactly with tuned 25% restart

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 8% of the time budget. Take the best packing, run SLSQP with maxiter 1000 and ftol=1e-15 starting from it (radii multiplied by 0.999999 so it is feasible), then repair with SHRINK=1e-12 instead of 1e-9. Keep the polished result only if its repaired sum is larger than the current best.
backlog.title: Final tight polish of best

backlog.spec: In the explore phase run SLSQP with maxiter 60 first. Compute the repaired sum. Continue to a full 200-iteration run from that point only if the repaired sum is within 0.03 of the best sum so far. Otherwise discard it. This frees time for more starts. Use the result of the continuation as the candidate.
backlog.title: Early abort of hopeless restarts

backlog.spec: For half of the fresh random starts, draw 13 random points with radii 0.05 and build the packing as point-symmetric about the square centre (the point p and the point 1-p), so n=26 gives 13 pairs. Add small noise sd 0.005 to break exact symmetry and run SLSQP as usual. Many good known packings are near-symmetric.
backlog.title: Symmetric-seeded starts

backlog.spec: For 40% of fresh starts, generate centres from a hex-like lattice with rows of 5 and 6 alternating (5,6,5,5,5 or similar giving 26 points) in [0.1,0.9]. Add Gaussian jitter sd 0.03 and a random subset of 3 circles moved to random positions. Use initial radius 0.08 and the standard SLSQP run.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice perturbed starts

backlog.spec: Change SLSQP pair constraints to d - ri - rj >= 1e-9 and wall constraints to c - r >= 1e-9, and set SHRINK to 0 in the repair. This should keep the optimum feasible so that the repair shrinks little, with the repair still applied as a safety net.
backlog.title: Margin-aware constraints

backlog.spec: After the 30% restart phase, do basin hopping from a current packing with Metropolis acceptance: accept a candidate with sum s' if s' > s or with probability exp((s'-s)/T) where T=0.002, decreasing linearly to 0.0002 by the end. Track the global best separately and return it. This differs from slot 28's fixed window because it uses a decaying temperature.
backlog.title: Basin hopping with Metropolis acceptance at temperature

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, perturb the best by deleting 3 random circles (set their radii to 0 and place at random locations), then first run SLSQP on only those 3 circles' centres and radii with the other circles fixed (a small 9-variable problem), then run the full SLSQP for 200 iterations. The small subproblem finds good insertion holes cheaply.
backlog.title: Grow-radius continuation from best

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, with probability 0.3 build a candidate from the best packing by reflecting it across a random axis (x, y or the diagonal) and replacing the circles in one half with the reflected circles of a different half, then fix the count to 26 by removing the smallest extras or adding small circles at random points. Run full SLSQP and accept only on improvement.
backlog.title: Mirror-half recombination hop

backlog.spec: Make no change to the logic of the current train.py beyond what is already in the incumbent (30% random restarts, then perturb the best packing with acceptance rule). The point is to spend a slot re-measuring the incumbent so that its true mean is known and later deltas are judged against a reliable baseline. If the file on hand lacks the slot 9 code, re-apply it: after 30% of the time, each iteration copies the best packing, relocates 2-3 random circles or adds centre noise sd 0.02, runs SLSQP, repairs, and keeps the result only if the radius sum improves.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent slot 9 unchanged

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 8% of the time budget. Take the best packing and run SLSQP with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter 1000, starting from the best centres with radii multiplied by 0.999. Repair the result and keep it only if its radius sum is larger. This squeezes out the residual slack left by the 200-iteration runs.
backlog.title: Final tight polish of best

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase keep a current packing and a best packing. Accept a hop result with probability exp((new_sum-cur_sum)/T), with T=0.002 decaying linearly to 0.0002 over the phase. Perturb the current packing, not the best. Always remember the best-ever packing and return it. This lets the search leave the local basin while staying close to good structures.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: For 40% of the explore restarts, generate centres symmetrically. Sample 13 random points, and mirror each through the square centre (x,y)->(1-x,1-y). Use initial radii of 0.05 plus small noise. SLSQP can break the symmetry as it optimizes, and many good packings of this problem are near-symmetric. The remaining restarts stay uniform random.
backlog.title: Symmetric-seeded starts

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, with probability 0.3 build the start by taking the best packing, scaling all radii by 0.8, and adding centre noise sd 0.01. Then run SLSQP. Shrinking the radii gives the circles room to rearrange, and SLSQP regrows them into a possibly different contact graph. The other hops stay as they are.
backlog.title: Grow-radius continuation from best

backlog.spec: Explore restarts run SLSQP for 40 iterations and measure the sum of radii of the unrepaired iterate. Continue to the full 200 iterations only if that sum is above the median of the previous 20 first-stage sums. Otherwise discard the run. The continuation uses the same x as the start. Note that earlier slots tried similar ideas with fixed thresholds, so use this relative median rule and keep the code short.
backlog.title: Cheap high-iteration restarts through early abort

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, with probability 0.2 build a start from the best packing. Keep the circles with x<0.5 and reflect them across x=0.5 to fill the right half. Then drop or add circles at random until there are exactly n, with new ones placed randomly with radius 0.02. Run SLSQP on this start. This explores symmetric variants of the best packing.
backlog.title: Mirror-half recombination hop

backlog.spec: For explore restarts, give SLSQP radius bounds that force a size structure: draw a random count k in 4..8 of circles whose radius upper bound is 0.2 and let the others have an upper bound of 0.09. Choose the bounded circles at random. Use the bounds only in the first 60 iterations, then lift them to [0,0.5] for the rest of the run, using a second minimize call from the result. This steers the restarts toward mixed-size layouts like the best known packing.
backlog.title: Small-circle count prior via fixed-size-class radius bounds

incumbent.description: After a 30% random-restart phase, spend the remaining time perturbing the best packing (relocate 2-4 circles or add sd 0.02 centre noise), re-optimizing with SLSQP and keeping improvements.

memo:
Helped: only slot 9 (30% random restarts, then perturbing the best packing with an acceptance rule): -2.6360, delta -0.0080, about 3.5 noise sd. It is a single run and has not been replicated, so it may be luck. Near misses, within noise of slot 9: slot 17 adaptive sd (-2.6354) and slot 28 walker (-2.6350). Weakly positive: slot 4 size-class start (-0.0024).

Did not help: SLSQP speed-ups and constraint forms (slots 0, 1, 2, 11), TIME_FRACTION 0.9, LP refit, staged jitter, remove-and-reinsert, short-iteration screening, alternative starts (sum r^p, Beta, lattice, pre-relaxation), swap and crossover moves, elite pools (+0.0092), always shaking (+0.0120), longer refinement maxiter, top-3 basin-hopping, and a 15% explore phase (-2.6318).

Next: 1) replicate slot 9 to confirm it. 2) Tune its perturbation size and restart fraction. 3) Combine it with the slot 4 start. 4) Skip micro-optimisations and further start-generation ideas.
